1.word_for_word: trayo-viṃśe — in the twenty-third chapter; tataḥ gopaiḥ anna-yācñā-apadeśataḥ — then, under the pretext of the cowherds' request for food; tat-patnī-anugrahāt — by favoring the sacrificers' wives; kṛṣṇaḥ dīkṣitān anvatāpayat — Kṛṣṇa caused the initiated sacrificers to repent
1.translation: In the twenty-third chapter, under the pretext of having the cowherd boys ask for food, Kṛṣṇa bestowed grace upon the sacrificers' wives and thereby caused the initiated sacrificers themselves to repent.

2.word_for_word: bhaktāyāḥ iti eka-vacanam — the singular form ‘of the devotee’; sadyaḥ sāyujya-abhiprāyeṇa — is used with reference to her immediately attaining sāyujya
2.translation: The singular ‘of the devotee’ is used because the passage has in view the one woman who immediately attained sāyujya.

4.word_for_word: asmad-visarjitāḥ — sent by us; āvābhyām prahitāḥ santaḥ yācadhvam — go and ask, having been dispatched by the two of us; yuṣmākam kā tatra lajjā — what embarrassment can there be for you; nanu tathāpi apātratvāt — objection: still, because we are unqualified recipients; asmabhyam kim iti dāsyanti — why should they give anything to us; tatra āha kīrtayantaḥ iti — he answers with the word ‘announcing [our names]’
4.translation: ‘Go and ask, for you have been sent by the two of us. What cause for embarrassment is there?’ One may object: ‘Even so, why would the sacrificers give food to us, who are not eligible recipients?’ The answer is given by the instruction to announce the names of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.

7.word_for_word: avidūre vartamānau — the two of us are staying nearby; vaḥ yat annam — the food belonging to you; tat laṣataḥ abhilāṣataḥ — we desire it; vaḥ odanam śraddhā ca yadi asti — if you have cooked food and faith; tarhi yacchata — then give it
7.translation: ‘The two of us are nearby and desire some of your food. If you possess both cooked food and faith, then give it.’

8.word_for_word: dīkṣitā vayam abhojya-annāḥ iti vadiṣyanti — they may say, ‘We are consecrated and our food may not yet be eaten’; svayam eva āśaṅkya āhuḥ — anticipating this objection, the boys reply; dīkṣāyā ārabhya — from the commencement of consecration; agnīṣomīya-paśu-ālambhanāt pūrvam — until before the offering of the Agnīṣomīya animal; doṣaḥ — the restriction applies; na tataḥ anyatra — not after that point; tathā sautramanyāḥ ca — and similarly in the Sautrāmaṇī; anyatra anyadā — except at its specifically restricted time
8.translation: Anticipating the response, ‘We are consecrated sacrificers and this food is not yet to be eaten,’ the boys explain the ritual rule: the restriction extends from the beginning of consecration until the Agnīṣomīya animal offering; outside that interval it does not apply. The Sautrāmaṇī likewise has its own particular restricted occasion.

9.word_for_word: kṣudre svarga-ādau āśā-mātram yeṣām — whose hope extends merely to insignificant goals such as heaven; bhūrīṇi kleśa-adhikāni karmāṇi yeṣām — whose numerous rites involve great hardship; ataḥ ajñāḥ — therefore ignorant; vṛthā jñāna-vṛddhā iti mānavantaḥ — proud of being learned only in vain
9.translation: Their hopes reached only to small rewards such as heaven, while their many ritual acts involved great hardship. Thus, although proud of being learned, they were in truth ignorant; their supposed maturity in knowledge was fruitless.

10.word_for_word: nanu karma-kramam ullaṅghya — objection: bypassing the prescribed order of ritual acts; ādeśa-kāle anya-artham annam anyasmai katham deyam — how can food assigned for a particular ritual moment and purpose be given to someone else; tatra āha deśa iti — this is answered by the verse beginning ‘place’; pṛthak caru-puroḍāśa-ādi-dravyam — the individual substances such as caru and sacrificial cakes; tantram — the ritual procedure; prayogaḥ — the performance; dharmaḥ — the unseen potency, apūrva
10.translation: One may object: ‘How can one disregard the ritual sequence and give to someone else food assigned to another purpose at a prescribed moment?’ The verse beginning with ‘place’ answers this. ‘Substance’ means the individual materials such as caru and sacrificial cakes; ‘tantra’ means the ritual procedure or performance; and ‘dharma’ here means the unseen ritual potency, the apūrva.

11.word_for_word: manuṣyaḥ ayam iti dṛṣṭyā — seeing him merely as ‘this is a human being’; martya-ātmānaḥ — regarding him as mortal; brāhmaṇā vayam mahāntaḥ iti manyamānāḥ — thinking ‘we brāhmaṇas are great’
11.translation: They looked upon Kṛṣṇa simply as a human being and regarded him as mortal, while thinking of themselves, ‘We are brāhmaṇas; we are great.’

13.word_for_word: laukikīm gatim — the ordinary way of the world; na hi kārya-arthinaḥ nirvidyante — those seeking to accomplish a task do not become discouraged; kaḥ vā yācakaḥ na parābhūyate — and what petitioner is not sometimes rebuffed; ity-ādi loka-sthitim darśayan — indicating such common worldly experience
13.translation: He points to ordinary worldly experience: one who has a task to accomplish does not give up merely because of a setback, and what petitioner has never been rebuffed?

14.word_for_word: kevalam dehena gṛhe vasanti — only with their bodies do they remain at home; dhiyā ca mayi eva uṣitāḥ — in mind they dwell in me alone; yataḥ mayi snigdhāḥ — because they are affectionate toward me; ataḥ dāsyanti — therefore they will give
14.translation: The wives remain in their homes only bodily; in their minds they dwell in me alone. Because they are affectionate toward me, they will give you the food.

17.word_for_word: saḥ kṛṣṇaḥ — that Kṛṣṇa; gopālaiḥ saha — together with the cowherd boys
17.translation: The pronoun refers to Kṛṣṇa together with the cowherd boys.

18.word_for_word: tat-kathā-ākṣipta-manastvāt — because their minds had been captivated by accounts of him; tat-darśana-utsukāḥ — eager to see him; tam upāgatam śrutvā — hearing that he had come; jāta-saṃśramāḥ — they immediately became intensely excited and hurried
18.translation: Their minds had already been captivated by hearing about Kṛṣṇa, so they longed to see him. As soon as they heard that he had come, they became intensely excited and hurried to him.

19.word_for_word: bhakṣya-bhojya-lehya-coṣya-bhedaiḥ catur-vidham — fourfold as chewable, regular food, lickable and suckable; bahu-guṇam — possessing many excellent qualities; saṃskāra-viśeṣaiḥ — by special preparations; rasa-saurabhya-ādayaḥ — taste, fragrance and the like; bhājanaiḥ amatraiḥ bhāṇḍaiḥ vā — in vessels or containers; pati-ādibhiḥ vāryamāṇā api — although restrained by husbands and others; priyam śrī-kṛṣṇam abhisasruḥ — they hastened toward their beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa; samudram nimnagā nadyaḥ iva — like rivers running down toward the ocean
19.translation: They brought food of the four kinds—foods to be chewed, eaten, licked and sucked—made excellent in taste, fragrance and other qualities by special preparation, and carried in vessels. Though their husbands and others tried to stop them, they hastened to their beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa, unobstructed like rivers flowing toward the ocean.

20.word_for_word: atra hetuḥ bhagavati iti — the reason is expressed by ‘toward Bhagavān’; dīrgham bahu-kālam — for a long time; śrutena śravaṇena — through what they had heard; dhṛta āśayaḥ yābhiḥ — they had fixed their intention upon him
20.translation: The cause of their irresistible movement is expressed by the phrase ‘toward Bhagavān’: over a long period of hearing about him, they had fixed their deepest intention upon him.

21.word_for_word: tathā-āgatāḥ satyaḥ — having come in this manner; dadṛśuḥ — they saw him
21.translation: Having come in this way, they beheld him.

22.word_for_word: hiraṇyavat paridhiḥ paridhānam yasya — whose garment was golden in appearance; pītāmbaram — meaning that he wore yellow cloth; vana-mālyaiḥ barhaiḥ dhātubhiḥ pravālaiḥ ca — with forest garlands, peacock feathers, mineral pigments and shoots; naṭavat veṣaḥ — dressed like an actor; anuvratasya sakhyuḥ aṃse vinyastaḥ hastaḥ — one hand resting upon the shoulder of a devoted friend; itareṇa hastena līlayā abjam dhunānam — with the other hand playfully twirling a lotus; karṇayoḥ utpale — lotuses at his ears; alakāḥ kapolayoḥ — curls upon his cheeks; mukha-abje hāsaḥ — a smile upon his lotus face
22.translation: ‘Golden-bordered garment’ means his yellow cloth. He was dressed like an actor with forest garlands, peacock feathers, mineral colors and fresh shoots. One hand rested upon the shoulder of a devoted friend, while with the other he playfully twirled a lotus. Lotuses adorned his ears, curls fell upon his cheeks, and a smile shone on his lotus face.

23.word_for_word: vṛtteḥ api layena sāmarasyaṃ āha — he describes complete harmony through the dissolution even of mental activity; prāya iti — with the verse beginning ‘prāyaḥ’; priya-tamasya udayāḥ utkarṣāḥ — the glories and excellences of their beloved; bahuśaḥ śrutāḥ — heard repeatedly; te eva karṇa-pūrāḥ — these themselves became ornaments filling the ears; kṛṣṇe nimagna-manasaḥ — with minds immersed in Kṛṣṇa; tam locana-dvāraiḥ antaḥ praveśya — bringing him within through the gateways of their eyes; suciram upaguhya — embracing him for a long time; tāpam jahuḥ — they abandoned their burning distress; aham-vṛttayaḥ prājñam parirabhya layaṃ prāpya yathā — like ego-functions merging upon embracing the deep-sleep witness
23.translation: He describes a state of complete harmony in which even ordinary mental activity dissolves. The many glories of their beloved that they had repeatedly heard became, as it were, ornaments filling and fulfilling their ears. Their minds submerged in Kṛṣṇa, they drew him inward through the gateways of their eyes, embraced him there for a long time, and cast off the heat of separation—just as the ego-functions dissolve into the witnessing consciousness in deep sleep.

24.word_for_word: akhila-dṛk-draṣṭā — the seer of all seeing; sarva-buddhi-sākṣī — witness of every mind; tāḥ tathā prāptāḥ vijñāya api — although knowing that they had come in this condition; tyakta-sarva-āśāḥ — having abandoned every other expectation; kevalam ātmanaḥ svasya eva didṛkṣayā — solely from the desire to see him himself
24.translation: Kṛṣṇa is the seer behind all seeing, the witness of every mind, and therefore fully knew the condition in which they had come. They had abandoned all other hopes and had come solely from the desire to see him.

25.word_for_word: he mahā-bhāgāḥ — O greatly fortunate ladies; vaḥ svāgatam — welcome to you; śubham āgamanam — your arrival is auspicious; pratibandha-tiraskāreṇa — overcoming all obstruction; asmākam didṛkṣayā prāptāḥ — you have come from desire to see us; idam vaḥ upapannam — this is fitting and proper for you
25.translation: ‘O greatly fortunate ladies, welcome; your coming is auspicious.’ Why so? Because, casting aside every obstacle, they had come solely from the desire to see him. Such conduct, he says, is fitting for them.

26.word_for_word: yuktatvam āha — he explains why it is fitting; ātma-priye — in me, who am both the Self and the beloved; kuśalāḥ vivekinaḥ — those who are wise and discriminating; svasyātmanaḥ artham puruṣārtham paśyanti — see the true goal of their own self; yathāvat bhaktim kurvanti — perform devotion properly; addhā sākṣāt — directly; ahaitukīm — without ulterior cause; phala-abhisandhi-rahitām — free from aim at a separate reward; avyavahitām — uninterrupted and unobstructed
26.translation: He explains why their conduct is fitting. The wise, who discern the true good of their own self, render devotion properly to him who is both the Self and the beloved. ‘Properly’ means directly, causelessly and without expectation of a separate result; therefore such devotion is also unobstructed and continuous.

27.word_for_word: ātmanaḥ sarvataḥ preṣṭhatvam upapādayati — he establishes that the Self is dearer than all else; prāṇa iti — by the verse beginning ‘life-breath’; svāḥ — one's relatives; jñātayaḥ — kinsmen; ātmā — the body; ete sarve yat-samparkāt — all these are dear because of relation to that Self; yasya adhyāsena upakaraṇatvena vā — through superimposition upon it or because they serve as its instruments
27.translation: He establishes that the Self is dearest of all. ‘One's own people’ means relatives, while ‘self’ in the verse can denote the body. Life, relatives and body are all dear only because of their relation to the true Self—either through identification with it or because they function as its instruments.

28.word_for_word: tat tasmāt kṛtārthāḥ yūyam — therefore you have attained your purpose; deva-yajanam yajña-vāṭam yāta — go to the place of sacrifice; nanu kṛtārthāḥ kim iti yāsyāmaḥ — objection: if we have attained our purpose, why should we go; patayaḥ pārayiṣyanti samāpayiṣyanti — your husbands will be able to complete the sacrifice; patīnām anugrahāya — this is for the sake of showing favor to the husbands
28.translation: ‘You have now attained your purpose; therefore return to the sacrificial enclosure.’ One may ask, ‘If our purpose is fulfilled, why return?’ Kṛṣṇa answers that their husbands must be enabled to complete the sacrifice. Their return is thus itself an act of grace toward those husbands.

29.word_for_word: nṛśaṃsam — cruel, harsh; nigamam — a promise or authoritative declaration; na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati — ‘my devotee does not perish’; vedam vā — or the Vedic declaration; na sa punar āvartate — ‘he does not return again’; pada-avasṛṣṭam — something cast down at the feet; avajñayā api dattam — even if given with apparent disregard; bahu-mānena keśaiḥ nivoḍhum — to bear it reverently upon the head/hair; dāsī-bhavitum — to become a maidservant
29.translation: ‘Nṛśaṃsam’ means harsh or cruel. ‘Nigama’ may mean the Lord's pledge, ‘My devotee does not perish,’ or the Vedic declaration, ‘He does not return again.’ Even something tossed contemptuously at his feet is to be taken up with the highest reverence upon one's head; their desire is simply to become his maidservants.

30.word_for_word: na gṛhṇanti naḥ asmān — they will not take us back; he arindama — O subduer of enemies; kāma-lobha-pāpa-ādi-damana — subduer of desire, greed, sin and the like; bhavataḥ prapadayoḥ patita-dehānām — for us whose bodies have fallen at the tips of your feet; anyā svarga-ādi-gatiḥ api na bhavet — let there be no other destination, even heaven and the like; tat dāsyam eva vidhehi — therefore appoint us only to service
30.translation: They continue: ‘Our families may no longer accept us. O subduer of enemies—of desire, greed, sin and all such foes—we have cast our bodies at your feet. Let us have no other destination, not even heaven. Grant us only your service.’

31.word_for_word: mayā upetāḥ — received or authorized by me; anujñātāḥ — permitted; pratyakṣam devān pradarśya — pointing out the gods visibly present; devāḥ api iti — ‘even the gods’
31.translation: ‘Received by me’ means ‘authorized and permitted by me.’ Kṛṣṇa then points to the deities present at the sacrifice and says, ‘Even the gods…’

32.word_for_word: tathāpi tvām tyaktum na śaknumaḥ iti cet — objection: even so, we cannot leave you; tatra āha na iti — he answers with the verse beginning ‘not’; prītaye — for pleasure; sukhāya — for happiness; anurāgāya — for love; sneha-vṛddhaye — for increase of affection; aṅga-saṅgaḥ — bodily contact; aṅgābhyām saṅgaḥ — contact of bodies
32.translation: If they object, ‘Even so, we cannot leave you,’ Kṛṣṇa replies with the verse beginning ‘not.’ Physical contact with him is not itself the sole cause of delight, happiness, love or the increase of affection; remembrance and devotion can produce these even in separation.

33.word_for_word: anasūyavaḥ — free from resentment; adoṣa-dṛṣṭayaḥ — not seeing fault
33.translation: ‘Anasūyavaḥ’ means that their relatives would no longer be resentful or see fault in them.

34.word_for_word: deham iti — concerning ‘the body’; tadīyam deham tatra vihāya — leaving her body there; caitanyena bhagavantam prāpa — in consciousness she attained Bhagavān
34.translation: The statement about her body means that she left that body there and, in consciousness, attained Bhagavān.

36.word_for_word: anuśīlayan — imitating, following in play; go-gopa-gopīnām iti karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī — the genitive ‘of cows, cowherds and gopīs’ is objective; rūpa-vāk-kṛtaiḥ — by form, speech and deeds; ramayan — delighting them; tān ramayitum reme — he sported in order to give them delight
36.translation: ‘Following’ here means playfully imitating. The genitive ‘of the cows, cowherds and gopīs’ is objective: through his form, speech and deeds he delighted them. Thus he sported for the purpose of giving them joy.

37.word_for_word: anusmṛti-prakāram āha — he explains the manner of their recollection; nara-anukaraṇavatoḥ viśveśvarayoḥ — of the Lords of the universe who appeared to imitate ordinary men; yācñām yat ahanma — that we rejected their request; kṛta-āgasaḥ vayam — we have committed an offense; iti anusmṛtya — remembering thus
37.translation: He explains the sacrificers' recollection: ‘Those two are the Lords of the universe, though they behaved like ordinary men, and we rejected their request. We have committed an offense.’ They remembered the event in this way.

38.word_for_word: bhāryāḥ gurūn iva mānayantaḥ — honoring their wives as though they were teachers; bhagavad-bhakti-rahitam ātmānam vyanindan — they condemned themselves as devoid of devotion to Bhagavān; dṛṣṭvā iti — this is expressed by ‘having seen’; alaukikīm — extraordinary; loka-atītām — beyond ordinary worldly conduct
38.translation: They now honored their own wives almost as teachers and condemned themselves for lacking devotion to Bhagavān. ‘Extraordinary’ means that the women's devotion had gone beyond ordinary worldly conduct.

39.word_for_word: tri-vṛt janma — threefold birth; śaukram — birth from semen; sāvitraṃ — the birth conferred by the Sāvitrī initiation; daikṣam — the birth through sacrificial consecration; vratam — celibate observance; brahmacaryam — brahmacarya; kriyāḥ — ritual acts; dākṣyam — ritual competence; dhig iti adhikṣepe — ‘fie!’ expresses condemnation; adhokṣaje vimukhāḥ — turned away from Adhokṣaja; janma-ādi tat sarvam dhig — all such birth and qualifications are worthless
39.translation: Their ‘threefold birth’ consists of physical birth, the second birth conferred by the Sāvitrī initiation, and the sacrificial birth through consecration. ‘Vow’ means brahmacarya; ‘rites and competence’ may be taken separately, or together as competence in ritual performance. Their cry ‘Fie!’ is self-condemnation: since they had turned away from Adhokṣaja, all their prestigious births, observances and ritual attainments were worthless.

42.word_for_word: dvijāti-saṃskāraḥ — the sacrament of the twice-born; upanayanam — initiation with the sacred thread; kriyāḥ — rites; sandhyā-upāsana-ādayaḥ — daily worship such as sandhyā
42.translation: ‘The sacrament of the twice-born’ means upanayana, and ‘rites’ includes practices such as the daily sandhyā worship.

46.word_for_word: ātmanaḥ doṣa-apavargeṇa — by removing their own faults; cāñcalya-garva-ādi-tyāgena — by abandoning fickleness, pride and the like
46.translation: This occurred through the removal of their own faults—through abandoning fickleness, pride and similar defects.

48.word_for_word: iti aśṛṇuma — ‘thus we heard’; evam sarvatra śrutavantaḥ vayam hi — indeed we had heard this teaching everywhere; tathā api — and yet, despite that
48.translation: ‘Thus we heard’ means: ‘We had indeed heard these truths repeatedly and from many sources, and yet even so we failed to act accordingly.’

52.word_for_word: na ca acalan — they did not move; tayoḥ darśanāya na jagmuḥ — they did not go to see the two Lords
52.translation: They nevertheless did not move from the sacrifice; they did not go to see Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.
